argmax.description: The accepted serial eight-expert argmax over a contiguous CUDA float32 row [8]. Outputs are rank-zero int32 selected and rank-zero float32 selected_probability. Initialize selected=0 and selected_probability=-infinity, then compare row[expert] strictly > selected_probability in expert order 0..7 and update both values only on success. This retains the earliest equal winner, skips NaNs by the original comparison, and retains (0,-infinity) if no comparison succeeds. The full row remains an explicit softmax-to-routing binding because routing uses row[selected] independently of the running selected_probability. The unchanged capacity tuple bypasses this read-only operation explicitly in the schedule. This is a separate proof target; exact replay does not establish upstream numerical equivalence or argmax stability between different score vectors.

projection.description: Accepted fixed-shape FlashMoE projection and its existing capacity-state initialization, ending immediately before the first token's softmax. Inputs: contiguous CUDA bfloat16 tokens [256,512] and explicit router weights [512,8], on the same device. Outputs: float32 scores [256,8], int32 counts [8], int64 token_indices [8,32], float32 probabilities [8,32], int32 survival [256,8]. Preserve the single 32-thread warp, BF16 register packing, mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.bf16.bf16.f32, zero float32 accumulators, token tiles 0..240 by 16, and k=0..496 by 16. The accepted serial initialization sets counts/survival to zero, indices to -1 and probabilities to positive zero. It is included here, not introduced as a separate prologue. The additional projection/softmax cut reflects the accepted bulk-MMA kernel followed by an interleaved serial token recurrence; it avoids interchanging softmax/argmax/routing across tokens. Scores remain immutable and explicitly feed every softmax occurrence; mutable state starts at the observed initialization boundary. No hidden weights, frozen tensor values or input mutation.

routing.description: One accepted serial selected-weight/capacity/routing update. Inputs 0..6 are contiguous same-device CUDA tensors: float32 row [8], rank-zero int32 selected, rank-zero float32 selected_probability, int32 previous counts [8], int64 previous token_indices [8,32], float32 previous probabilities [8,32], int32 previous survival [256,8]. Input7 is the token position in [0,256). Selected must be in [0,8); previous state is the full initialized state for token 0 or the preceding token's produced state, with nonnegative demand counts and the original token order. Preserve combine_weight=__fadd_rn(0.0f,selected_probability) and probability=fdividef(row[selected],combine_weight), without replacing the division by one or skipping arithmetic for dropped tokens. Use rank=counts[selected]++ even on drops; only rank<32 writes the selected token slot, probability and survival flag. Outputs are the COMPLETE updated counts [8], token_indices [8,32], probabilities [8,32], survival [256,8], with all untouched entries retained, in new allocations without input-alias mutation. The original kernel snapshots these arrays after each token; its final count-publication loop makes the last counts the expert_demand output, so no epilogue family is invented. Scalar token position is an explicit schedule parameter; scores remain available from projection for the next softmax. This family is numerical because it retains the selected weight arithmetic as well as capacity indexing.

softmax.description: One accepted serial online softmax for explicit token position input1 in [0,256), reading contiguous CUDA float32 scores input0 [256,8]. Output: the complete normalized float32 row [8]. Initialize maximum to -infinity and denominator to positive zero; visit experts 0..7 with fmaxf, __fsub_rn, __expf and __fmaf_rn in their original recurrence order, then normalize experts 0..7 with __fdividef. No alternative softmax, reassociation, reduction or parallel scalar work. Observe the local row immediately after normalization inside the original router_capacity kernel. Maximum and denominator are dead beyond this cut. The complete counts/indices/probabilities/survival tuple is unchanged during softmax and argmax and flows directly from the previous routing observation (or projection initialization) to the next routing occurrence; the immutable scores also remain explicit. The row flows unchanged to both argmax and routing.
